chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Hamzah ibn al-Qasim al-Alavi narrated that Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Imran al-Barqi narrated that Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamdani narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Abdillah and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon them both), who said:

If the Riser (al-Qa'im) were to rise, he would rule with three rulings that no one before him had ruled with: he would kill the fornicating old man, and he would kill the one who withholds the alms-tax, and he would cause a brother to inherit his brother regarding the shade-producers.

key_terms.الْأَخَ أَخَاهُ: A brother inheriting from his brother
key_terms.الْأَظِلَّةِ: Shade-producers (typically referring to date palms or orchards)
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser, a title for the Mahdi
key_terms.مَانِعَ الزَّكَاةِ: The one who withholds the alms-tax

ai.seo_question: What are the three unique legal rulings that the Mahdi will implement upon his rise?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the Mahdi's authority to introduce novel legal precedents (ahkam jadida) that were not established by previous prophets, emphasizing the dynamic nature of Shia jurisprudence. The three decrees—capital punishment for the elderly fornicator, execution for zakat withholdors, and a unique inheritance rule for siblings in shaded groves—demonstrate his comprehensive governance over both ritual and civil matters. These rulings reflect the Imams' view that the Mahdi will restore justice by applying specific divine wisdoms that were previously suspended or less emphasized.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-223 Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Hamzih ibn al-Qasim al-Alavi quoted Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Imran al-Barqy, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamedany, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Hamzih, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) and Abil-Hassan (MGB),

“Once the Riser (MGB) uprises, he (MGB) will issue three decrees which no one has issued before him. He will order that any fornicating old man be killed. He will order that anyone who prohibits the alms-tax be killed. And he will order that a man’s brothers should inherit from whatever property that produces a shade.”
